title: VIABLE teaching settings (How the AI helps)
description: An activity's teaching settings: the teacher's goal, a K-12 standard or a durable skill as it was chosen, how far the AI may go, what the teacher wants to hear about, misconceptions to listen for, and a section's own help level and note. The agent is given the goal, the standard and the help level as instructions with its reply steps (VETTING's reviewer checks them too) and as context.workspace.teaching; watch_for stays with the teacher. An instruction, not a guarantee.

help.description: ask_first: ask what the learner thinks first and build on it; hint: hints and guiding questions, no answers; step_up: ask first, then hints, then a worked example with other numbers once they have really tried; explain: explain and show a worked example when stuck, then let them try; check_only: only check the learner's own work.

defaults.description: Where the teacher chose no misconceptions or guidance, whether the common misconceptions of the goal and research that suits how much the AI does are chosen for them (defaults.js), each marked by: default in a turn's record. false: only what the teacher chose. Left out: on in the Harness, on a server of your own and on the Learning Platform's teacher's door; off on the VIABLE Developer Platform, so a study's settings never change.

ladder.description: For the level step_up: when each kind of help comes, decided by code from how many times the learner has tried, in place of leaving the moment to the model (policy.js). true takes the usual ladder. Left out: the level's own words say when, and the model decides.

hint_after.description: Earlier tries before a hint is given. Default 1. A learner who says they are stuck gets a hint sooner.

example_after.description: Earlier tries before a worked example with different numbers is shown. Default 2, and always after hint_after.

turn_brief.description: Whether a reply starts from what this moment needs (the teacher's goal and limit, a teaching move, only the parts this message calls for) in place of all these settings. Left out: on in the Harness and on a server of your own, off on VIABLE.

tools_off.description: Tools the AI may not use in this activity, by name: an agent's web, knowledge, memory or agents, or a tool of the app's own.

misconceptions.description: Misconceptions the teacher chose to listen for (Eedi Misconceptions Graph, CC BY 4.0), each kept as it was chosen with the construct it hinders.

guidance.description: Guidance chosen from others' research (a context component's items), each kept as it was chosen with what it is for and where it came from. A turn's brief takes at most two that fit the moment.

when.description: The moments it is for. Left out, it comes when what was said shares words with it.

about.description: Words saying what it applies to, which what was said is compared with instead of its text.

component.description: The component it came from, as id@version.

sections.description: A section's own help level, note and moments the AI writes first at, by section ID, applied over the activity's for that section's learners only.

oneOf.description: The AI never writes first for this section.

role.description: Who the AI is in this activity, when it plays someone: a skeptic, a beginner to teach, someone in a scene.

design.description: Which design from research the activity is built on, for the teacher to read. It does not go to the AI.

watch_for.description: What the teacher wants to hear about. Never sent to the AI.

speaks_up.description: When the AI writes first, unasked: the moments the learner's page watches for, each only where set, at most `most` times in a step and `gap` minutes apart, which the server holds to. The page sends which moment it was, never the learner's words.

minutes.description: Minutes without writing, answering or asking anything on a step, with the page open.

say.description: What the AI does at this moment, in the teacher's or researcher's words, in place of the move from research.

minutes.description: Minutes working on the step without writing to the AI.

after.description: Which wrong answer to a question: 1 for the first, 2 for the second.

words.description: New words of writing since the AI last looked, at a pause.

say.description: What the AI does at this moment, in the teacher's or researcher's words, in place of the move from research.

how.description: ask: asks how it is going; point: points to one place to look again, as a question; fix: names one or two things to fix and what to change.

focus.description: What a note on their writing is about: spelling and grammar, ideas and structure, or what makes it good. Left out: whatever matters most.

handed_in.description: Writing handed in. true is the same as {}.

most.description: At most this many times in a step (default 2).

gap.description: At least this many minutes apart (default 3).

reviewer_reads.description: message: a VETTING reviewer reads the learner's message too, as data. Left out: only the reply. A reviewer step's own reviewer_reads wins.

standard.description: A standard from Learning Commons' Knowledge Graph, or a durable skill (Carnegie Skills Progressions) at a level, kept as it was chosen with the attribution CC BY 4.0 requires. Runs read this copy and never call Learning Commons.

level.description: For a skill: the level learners work toward.

prior.description: The standards before it (for a skill, the level below).

source.description: Where it came from, with the attribution statements CC BY 4.0 asks to carry along.
